I appreciate you sharing that, and I don't doubt that many people have genuinely positive experiences. But I think there's a difference between individual benefit and societal impact. Someone can feel more connected to their friends while the platform itself is eroding attention spans, amplifying misinformation, and making people more anxious on average. Those two things coexist.

The fact that most people you've spoken to see it as a net positive doesn't surprise me — that's actually consistent with my point. Platforms are designed to feel good in the moment, which makes it harder to see the cumulative harm. I'm not going to change my view just because it's uncommon. The evidence on attention fragmentation and adolescent mental health is pretty clear, and "everyone else thinks differently" isn't an argument against data. I'm happy to discuss specifics if you disagree with the evidence itself.
